security_audit.summary: All 218 static detections are false positives in Markdown documentation and illustrative configuration. The material describes plugin structures, safe path constraints, and optional command examples; it contains no executable implementation, hidden data collection, or prompt-injection language. No semantic security findings were identified.

remediation.issue: Examples show environment-variable credentials in MCP configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders in documentation and advise plugin authors to grant the minimum required credentials only to trusted MCP servers.

remediation.issue: Examples include shell commands and hook scripts for plugin authors.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as user-reviewed templates and recommend fixed arguments, input validation, and least-privilege execution for real hooks.

content.user_title: Design a Claude Code Plugin Structure
content.value_statement: Plugin projects can become inconsistent when manifests, commands, agents, skills, hooks, and MCP settings are placed without clear rules. This skill provides documented layouts, naming guidance, and portable configuration patterns for building maintainable Claude Code plugins.
actual_capabilities: Describes standard directories for commands, agents, skills, hooks, scripts, and references.
Shows component auto-discovery and file naming conventions.
Provides manifest examples for plugin metadata, custom paths, hooks, and MCP configuration.
Offers minimal, standard, and advanced plugin structure examples.
limitations: Does not create files or install a plugin by itself.
Does not validate a completed plugin against a runtime.
Examples require review and adaptation for project-specific security needs.
Does not provide credentials or configure external MCP services.

use_cases.title: Start a new plugin
use_cases.description: Plan a minimal plugin folder layout and manifest before adding components.

use_cases.title: Organize a growing plugin
use_cases.description: Move commands, agents, skills, hooks, scripts, and references into predictable locations.

use_cases.title: Review plugin configuration
use_cases.description: Check manifest paths, discovery rules, and portable path references before sharing a plugin.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: plan a minimal plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a minimal Claude Code plugin structure for a documentation helper. Include the manifest location and required files.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: add components
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Claude Code plugin layout with two commands, one agent, one skill, and hooks. Explain where each file belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: configure custom paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed plugin layout and recommend manifest custom paths. Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} for all internal references.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: security-focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-release checklist for my Claude Code plugin. Cover manifest paths, hook safety, MCP credential handling, and component discovery.

output_examples.input: I need a plugin with one command and one skill.
output: Place the command Markdown file in commands and the skill in its own skills subdirectory.

output_examples.input: How should I reference a script from a hook?
output: Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} to form the internal script path.
Keep the manifest path relative where required.
Review shell arguments and permissions before enabling the hook.

output_examples.input: Can I store MCP settings in the plugin?
output: Use the documented plugin-local MCP configuration pattern when appropriate.
Only configure trusted MCP servers with the minimum required access.

best_practices: Keep the manifest small and place components in their standard directories.
Use descriptive kebab-case names for commands, agents, and skills.
Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} for internal paths and review every hook before use.
anti_patterns: Do not place component folders inside .claude-plugin unless the manifest explicitly supports that layout.
Do not use hardcoded absolute paths or home-directory shortcuts for plugin resources.
Do not copy credential placeholders into a plugin without least-privilege review.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It explains how to organize and configure Claude Code plugin projects.

faq.question: Where does plugin.json belong?
faq.answer: Place it in the .claude-plugin directory at the plugin root.

faq.question: Which components can a plugin include?
faq.answer: A plugin can include commands, agents, skills, hooks, scripts, references, and MCP configuration.

faq.question: Why use CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT?
faq.answer: It makes references to internal plugin files portable across installation locations.

faq.question: Does this skill install plugins?
faq.answer: No. It provides structure and configuration guidance only.

faq.question: Are the shell and credential examples ready to use?
faq.answer: No. Review and adapt every example, especially hooks, commands, external services, and credentials.
